pages.text: When quality is enabled, curing combines the leaf's Growth Quality with the cure method, environmental consistency, interruptions, mixed-method penalties, wet damage, and a small random bonus. Finished curing is normally capped at $(item)100$() quality.

Processed-tobacco tiers are:$(br2)$(4)0–30 Poor$()$(br)31–60 Common$(br)61–80 Good$(br)81–89 Excellent$(br)$(2)90–100 Perfect$()$(br)$(2)101–120 Exceptional$()$(br2)Exceptional scores are reached later through fermentation/aging; the curing step itself caps at 100.
pages.title: Quality Tiers

pages.text: If a valid cure stops after previously running, the rack records an interruption. Switching between cure methods can also create a mixed-method batch. Small amounts of mixing are less severe than a batch split heavily between methods.
pages.title: Interruptions & Mixing

pages.text: Direct rain is dangerous. Every 200 ticks of direct rain exposure adds wet damage. When the rain-exposure counter reaches $(4)1,200 ticks$()—60 seconds at uninterrupted exposure—the batch is ruined into Spoiled Tobacco. Once sheltered, the counter falls by $(item)5 ticks per game tick$().
pages.title: Rain Damage

pages.text: For high-end tobacco, load the rack before it reaches 10%, keep one cure method valid from start to finish, and keep the batch dry. Spectacles make it easy to catch a paused rack before an interruption becomes a long one.
